pool.text: Yokohama opened for trade with the West following the end of the seclusion policy.
The Port of Yokohama was officially opened on June 2.
Japan's first English language newspaper, the Japan Herald, was published.
The first ice cream confectionery and beer were produced in Japan.
A great fire destroyed much of the foreign settlement in Yokohama.
Western influence and technological transfer contributed to establishing Japan's first daily newspaper.
Yamashita Park on the waterfront opened, utilizing rubble from the quake.
The first bombing of the city occurred in the Doolittle Raid.
Thousands died when B-29s firebombed the city in the Great Yokohama Air Raid.
The city was designated by government ordinance on September 1.
The city's tram and trolleybus system was abolished alongside subway expansion.
Construction of Minato Mirai 21 urban development project started on reclaimed land.
Minato Mirai 21 hosted the Yokohama Exotic Showcase featuring maglev trains.
The film Mothra took place in Yokohama.
Minato Mirai 21 saw the opening of the Yokohama Landmark Tower.
The city incorporated the Fourth Tokyo International Conference on African Development.
The city marked the 150th anniversary of the port opening.
From Up on Poppy Hill animated film was set in the Yamate district.
APM Terminals Yokohama facility was recognized as the most productive container terminal.
Yokohama's total gross regional product decreased due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
